title: Effects of Meditation and Music Listening on Brain Activity and Behavior in Healthy Adults
official: Differential Effects of Focused Attention Meditation, Loving-Kindness Meditation, and Music Listening on Electroencephalographic (EEG) Activity and Behavioral Performance in Healthy Adults
summary:
This study aims to determine whether two types of meditation affect brain activity, attention, and emotional responses differently from listening to relaxing instrumental music in healthy adults.

The main questions are:

* Does focused attention meditation produce greater improvements in attention and related brain activity than loving-kindness meditation or listening to music?
* Does loving-kindness meditation produce different patterns of brain activity related to emotional processing and improve the ability to respond to negative emotional information?

Researchers plan to enroll 69 healthy adults aged 18 to 59. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: focused attention meditation, loving-kindness meditation, or listening to neutral instrumental music.

Each participant will complete one laboratory visit. During this visit, participants will:

* Complete recordings of brain activity using electroencephalography (EEG), a noninvasive method that measures electrical activity from sensors placed on the scalp.
* Complete a computerized attention task before and after the intervention.
* Listen to a 15-minute guided meditation or music recording, according to their assigned group.
* Complete a picture-viewing task in which they evaluate everyday images and, on some trials, try to interpret them less negatively.

Researchers will compare changes in brain activity and attention, as well as responses to the pictures, across the three groups.

The findings may help clarify whether different meditation practices produce distinct short-term effects on brain function, attention, and emotional processing.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 to 59 years.
* Able to understand study instructions and provide informed consent in English.
* Right-hand dominant.
* Normal or corrected-to-normal vision and hearing.
* No regular meditation practice exceeding 75 minutes per week during the previous three months.
* Able to participate in a laboratory session involving EEG recordings, computerized attention tasks, and listening to a 15-minute audio recording.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of neurological disorders or stroke.
* History of traumatic brain injury or brain surgery within the previous five years that affected thinking, memory, or motor function.
* History of bipolar disorder or schizophrenia.
* Severe depression or anxiety.
* Pregnancy.
* Left-hand dominance.
* Uncorrected vision or hearing impairments that could interfere with the study procedures.
* Regular cigarette smoking or nicotine vaping.
* Regular meditation practice exceeding 75 minutes per week during the previous three months.

Use of medications that may affect mood, cognition, or alertness, including antidepressants, anti-anxiety medications, antipsychotics, anti-seizure medications, and prescription sleep medications, is not an exclusion criterion. You may still collect medication information through the health questionnaire.
